11.1.4. Macaque atlas:  the CHARM¶
Charm is more valuable than beauty. You can resist beauty, but you
can’t resist charm. –Audrey Tautou
Overview¶
Here we present the Cortical Hierarchy Atlas of the Rhesus Macaque
(CHARM).
This atlas is defined in the coordinates/space of the NMT v2
template, described here:
Macaque template:  NMT v2 (current).
Contents¶
The CHARM parcellates the macaque cortex at six spatial scales. The
finest level is based on the D99 atlas, while the broadest level forms
four cortical lobes. Between these levels, regions are progressively
grouped to form increasingly large composite structures. This allows
the researcher to choose the appropriate scale of investigation for
their study design and data.
Example of the CHARM hierarchical structure¶
Tree diagram showing successively finer parcellation of the
inferior temporal cortex (from Jung et al., 2021)
The CHARM is distributed as a single data set with six
sub-volumes. Note that for the purpose of using AFNI sub-brick
selectors, CHARM Level 1 is volume "[0]" and Level 6 is volume
"[5]", because AFNI (like Python and C) use zero-base counting.
The CHARM is distributed with the NMT v2. The NMT v2 has several forms
and variants (based on symmetry/asymmetry, FOV and voxel size), and
for each of these there is an accompanying CHARM.
Note that the NMT download also includes a CSV table file of the ROI
labels, hierarchically organized.  This can be viewed as a simple text
file or within any spreadsheet software, such as shown in the
following image.
Snippet of the CHARM hierarchical data table¶
Part of the CHARM ROI organizational table text file included
in NMT download
Example images¶
The following images were made using the symmetric NMT v2 template
(with “standard” spatial resolution = 0.25 mm, and FOV = brain volume)
and accompanying CHARM.
Skull-stripped NMT with the CHARM (level 1)
Skull-stripped NMT with the CHARM (level 2)
Skull-stripped NMT with the CHARM (level 3)
Skull-stripped NMT with the CHARM (level 4)
Skull-stripped NMT with the CHARM (level 5)
Skull-stripped NMT with the CHARM (level 6)
The script used to make these images with ``@chauffeur_afni`` is
available here: do_view_charm.tcsh.
Download¶
The CHARM is distributed as part of the NMT v2 download. For each
form/variant of the NMT, there is a matching CHARM dataset, as well.
To download and unpack the datasets, please see the instructions...
... here for the symmetric form:
Download symmetric NMT v2 datasets
... here for the asymmetric form:
Download asymmetric NMT v2 datasets
Citation/questions¶
If you make use of the CHARM and/or accompanying NMT v2 data in your
research, please cite:
Jung, B., Taylor, P.A., Seidlitz, J., Sponheim, C., Perkins P.,
Ungerleider, L.G., Glen, D., Messinger, A. (2021)  “A comprehensive
macaque fMRI pipeline and hierarchical atlas.” NeuroImage, submitted.
https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2020.08.05.237818v1
Reveley C, Gruslys A, Ye FQ, Glen D, Samaha J, E Russ B, Saad Z, K
Seth A, Leopold DA, Saleem KS (2017). Three-Dimensional Digital
Template Atlas of the Macaque Brain. Cereb Cortex 27(9):4463-4477.
doi: 10.1093/cercor/bhw248.
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6075609/
For questions, comments and/or suggestions, contact:
Adam.

11.1.5. Macaque atlas:  the SARM¶
Overview¶
Here we present the Subcortical Atlas of the Rhesus Macaque
(SARM).
This atlas is defined in the coordinates/space of the NMT v2
template, described here:
Macaque template:  NMT v2 (current).
Contents¶
Digitized anatomical atlases are crucial for examining brain structure
and the functional networks identified by magnetic resonance imaging
(MRI). To aid in MRI data analysis, we created a complete parcellation
of the rhesus macaque subcortex using high-resolution ex vivo structural
imaging and histological data. The structural scan was warped to the NIMH
Macaque Template (NMT v2), an in vivo population template, where the
parcellation was refined to produce the Subcortical Atlas of the Rhesus
Macaque (SARM). The NMT v2 has several forms and variants (based on
symmetry/asymmetry, FOV and voxel size), and for each of these there is
an accompanying SARM.
Using an updated version of the Rhesus Monkey Brain in Stereotaxic
Coordinates  (Paxinos et al., 2009; Paxinos et al., in preparation) for
guidance, the SARM features 6 parcellation levels, arranged
hierarchically from fine regions-of-interest (ROIs) to broader composite
regions, suited for fMRI studies.
The SARM is distributed as a single dataset with six sub-volumes. Note
that for the purpose of using AFNI sub-brick selectors, SARM Level 1 is
volume “[0]” and Level 6 is volume “[5]”, because AFNI (like Python and
C) use zero-base counting.
Note that the NMT v2.0 download also includes a CSV table file of the
ROI labels, hierarchically organized. This can be viewed as a simple
text file or within any spreadsheet software, such as shown in the
following image.
Example images¶
The following images were made using the symmetric NMT v2 template (with
“standard” spatial resolution = 0.25 mm, and FOV for the SARM atlas) and
accompanying SARM.
NMT underlay with the SARM (level 1) overlaid
NMT underlay with the SARM (level 2) overlaid
NMT underlay with the SARM (level 3) overlaid
NMT underlay with the SARM (level 4) overlaid
NMT underlay with the SARM (level 5) overlaid
NMT underlay with the SARM (level 6) overlaid
The script used to make these images with ``@chauffeur_afni`` is
available here: do_view_sarm.tcsh.
Download¶
The SARM is distributed as part of the NMT v2 download using @Install_NMT
(See the instructions for the NMT installation below).
The SARM atlas is available only in the symmetric NMT space.
To download and unpack the datasets together with the NMT template and atlases,
please see these instructions...
... here for the symmetric form:
Download symmetric NMT v2 datasets
You may download the SARM datasets separately, from the AFNI website
using the links below.
* (the plain Linux-y terminal way) copy+paste:
curl -O https://afni.nimh.nih.gov/pub/dist/atlases/macaque/SARM/SARM.tgz
tar -xvf SARM.tgz
(the mouseclick+ way) click on this link,
... and then unpack the zipped directory by either clicking on it
or using the above tar command.
AFNI environment variables¶
The @Install_NMT script automatically adds AFNI environment variables to use
the SARM atlas, but these can beThese variables can be configured in your .afnirc
file in your home directory to take advantage of the SARM atlas for “whereami”,
“Show atlas colors

11.1.2. Macaque template:  NMT v2 (current)¶
Overview¶
Here we present the NIMH Macaque Template (NMT), version 2.0. This is
a group template from 31 macaques with surfaces and a 5-class tissue
segmentation.
The NMT v2 is the most current version of this dataset.
Be sure to also check out the accompanying CHARM (Cortical Hierarchy
Atlas of the Rhesus Macaque) dataset, described
here.
Contents¶
There are both symmetric and asymmetric “variants” for the NMT v2.
Additionally, for each variant there are sets of data with different
spatial resolution and FOV:
the “standard” NMT has 0.25 mm isotropic voxels and a
“brain-focused” FOV,
the “low-res” NMT has 0.5 mm isotropic voxels and a “brain-focused”
FOV,
the “full-head” NMT has 0.25 mm isotropic voxels and a larger FOV,
encompassing more non-brain material.
An example of the contents in the download of the symmetric NMT v2
(which is essentially mirrored in the asymmetric version) is provided
here:
NMT v2 contents
Description
NMT_v2.0_sym/
directory of the “standard” NMT files (i.e., standard spatial
resolution of 0.25 mm iso voxels and brain-focused FOV)
NMT_v2.0_sym_05mm/
directory of the “low-res” NMT files (0.5 mm iso voxels; lower
spatial resolution but still useful, if not preferred, for some
analysis cases like in standard FMRI processing)
NMT_v2.0_sym_fh/
directory of the “full head” NMT files (i.e., 0.25 mm iso
voxels but a larger FOV, more non-brain material), which may be
useful for some alignment cases
NMT_v2.0_sym_surfaces/
directory of GIFTI surfaces of many of the tissue/segmentation
regions
CustomAtlases.niml
atlas description text file for AFNI
NMT_changelog.txt
text file of changes and updates to the distributed datasets
NMT_v2.0_sym_env.csh
script to set AFNI environment variables for AFNI to use
atlases and make AFNI more monkey friendly.  Note: running
this script will change your default atlases for whereami
functionality, so if you also do human studies, be aware that
you might have to change some environment settings again later.
supplemental_CHARM/
directory of tables of CHARM ROI index/label definitions and more
supplemental_D99/
directory of a table of D99 ROI index/label definitions
An example of the contents of the “standard” NMT directory
NMT_v2.0_sym/, above are as follows (within similar sets of data
in the “low-res” and “full-head” directories):
NMT_v2.0_sym/ contents
Description
CHARM_in_NMT_v2.0_sym.nii.gz
hierarchical atlas (6 levels) in NMT v2 space
D99_atlas_in_NMT_v2.0_sym.nii.gz
D99 atlas in NMT v2 space
NMT_v2.0_sym_brainmask.nii.gz
binary brain mask (including cerebellum)
NMT_v2.0_sym_GM_cortical_mask.nii.gz
binary mask of cortical GM
NMT_v2.0_sym.nii.gz
the NMT v2 template, with non-brain material surrounding

Download symmetric NMT v2 datasets¶
You can download and unpack the symmetric variant/form of the NMT
v2 in any of the following ways:
(the AFNI way) copy+paste:
@Install_NMT -nmt_ver 2.0 -sym sym
(the plain Linux-y terminal way) copy+paste:
curl -O https://afni.nimh.nih.gov/pub/dist/atlases/macaque/nmt/NMT_v2.0_sym.tgz
tar -xvf NMT_v2.0_sym.tgz
(the mouseclick+ way) click on this link,
... and then unpack the zipped directory by either clicking on it
or using the above tar command.
Download asymmetric NMT v2 datasets¶
You can download and unpack the asymmetric variant/form of the NMT
v2 in any of the following ways:
(the AFNI way) copy+paste:
@Install_NMT -nmt_ver 2.0 -sym asym
(the Linux-y terminal way) copy+paste:
curl -O https://afni.nimh.nih.gov/pub/dist/atlases/macaque/nmt/NMT_v2.0_asym.tgz
tar -xvf NMT_v2.0_asym.tgz
(the mouseclick+ way) click on this link,
... and then unpack the zipped directory by either clicking on it
or using the above tar command.

metadata.source_quote: an 'outer surface' surface file is created, called ?h.outer-pial-smoothed, which is basically an 'enveloped' version of the (pial) input. It is created by a morphological closing operation

nodes.name: Extract the main component and smooth the outer surface using mris_extract_main_component and mris_smooth.

metadata.source_quote:
?h.pial-outer-main
mris_smooth -nw -n 30
?h.pial-outer-smoothed

nodes.name: Convert the outer smoothed surface to ASCII normals using mris_convert.

metadata.source_quote:
?h.pial-outer-smoothed
mris_convert -n (output normals as ascii)
?h.pial-outer-smoothed-normals.asc

nodes.name: Find corresponding centers between pial and outer smoothed surfaces using find_corresponding_center_FSformat.

metadata.source_quote:
?h.pial, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed
find_corresponding_center_FSformat
?h.pial.*.center

nodes.name: Define circular regions of interest on the outer surface using make_roi_paths in MATLAB.

metadata.source_quote:
?h.pial, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed.asc
make_roi_paths
?h.pial.*.path

nodes.name: Convert paths to labels using mri_path2label.

metadata.source_quote:
?h.pial.*.path, ?h.pial.*.center
mri_path2label
?h.pial.*.label

nodes.name: Compute lGI values using compute_lgi in MATLAB and convert the result to the final surface file with mris_convert.

metadata.source_quote:
?h.pial, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed-normals.asc, ?h.pial.*.labels, ?h.pial-outer-smoothed-mesh
compute_lgi
?h.pial_lgi.asc

nodes.name: Check for topological defects of the pial surface using mris_euler_number, as defects cause mris_compute_lgi to crash.

metadata.source_quote: In case of topological defects of the pial surface (run mris_euler_number), mris_compute_lgi crashes.

nodes.name: If mris_compute_lgi crashes due to topological defects, simply relaunching it is usually sufficient to overcome the issue.

metadata.source_quote: Usually, simply relaunching mris_compute_lgi is sufficient to overcome this issue.

nodes.name: Files named lh.pial_lgi and rh.pial_lgi in the subject's surf directory, containing lGI values at each vertex of the pial surface.

metadata.source_quote: This will produce files named lh.pial_lgi and rh.pial_lgi in the subjects surf directory.

nodes.name: The primary output file ?h.pial_lgi can be viewed as an overlay in tksurfer or freeview.

metadata.source_quote: The primary output file is ?h.pial_lgi, which can be viewed as an overlay in tksurfer or freeview

nodes.name: The output can be used for vertex-wise analysis in QDEC after sampling to fsaverage.

metadata.source_quote: To perform a vertex-wise analysis in QDEC of the lgi surface data, first sample the results to the average template subject 'fsaverage'

nodes.name: ROI-based statistics can be generated using mri_segstats with the pial_lgi file.

metadata.source_quote:
It is also possible to generate statistics on ROIs, for example:
mri_segstats --annot my_subject_id lh aparc --i $SUBJECTS_DIR/my_subject_id/surf/lh.pial_lgi --sum lh.aparc.pial_lgi.stats

nodes.name: Diameter of the structural element sphere used in morphological closing; decreasing below 10mm produces an outer surface entering sulci, increasing does not substantially affect morphology but increases computation time.

metadata.source_quote: Decreasing the diameter of the se sphere below 10mm will produce an outer surface entering in the sulci. Increasing it does not substantially affect the morphology of the outer surfaces (but increase computation time!).

nodes.name: Number of smoothing iterations for mris_smooth is set to 30.

metadata.source_quote: mris_smooth -nw -n 30

nodes.name: The structural element size for make_outer_surface is set to 15.

metadata.source_quote: make_outer_surface -se 15

nodes.name: CIVET-Macaque cortical surface reconstruction and quality controls

metadata.purpose: Automated extraction of cortical surfaces and evaluation of cortical thickness from macaque T1-weighted MR images, with surface-based registration and quality controls.

nodes.name: T1-weighted MR scan of a macaque brain as the primary input.

metadata.source_quote: CIVET takes as input a T1w scan and registers if to standardized space, herein the NMT

nodes.name: Optional T2-weighted or proton density scans for multimodal tissue classification.

metadata.source_quote: with the possibility of a multimodal classification should T2-weighted and/or proton density scans be available

nodes.name: NMT brain mask and tissue priors for registration and classification.

metadata.source_quote: Registration, using minctracc, proceeds by specifying the brain mask on the target image only, herein the NMT volume with its associated brain mask

nodes.name: The pipeline is designed for macaque brains and uses a length scale of 0.4 relative to human brain size.

metadata.source_quote: A length scale of 0.4 was derived from the cubic root of the macaque-to-human volume ratio

nodes.name: Processing is performed in the NMT standardized space.

metadata.source_quote: Processing is performed based on the NIMH Macaque Template (NMT), as the reference template

nodes.name: The pipeline requires T1w scans; T2-weighted or proton density scans are optional for multimodal classification.

metadata.source_quote: relies on the T1w scan, with the possibility of a multimodal classification should T2-weighted and/or proton density scans be available

nodes.name: The NMT v2 is the current version of the template, with symmetric and asymmetric variants and multiple resolutions.

metadata.source_quote: The NMT v2 is the most current version of this dataset.

nodes.name: Resample the image into NMT space at 0.25 or 0.50 mm isotropic resolution.

metadata.source_quote: The macaque brain is resampled in linear standardized space at the processing voxel resolution of 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm

nodes.name: Mask the brain using FSL bet with intensities sampled within the template brain mask.

metadata.source_quote: Brain-masking is based on extensions of FSL bet version 1 (Smith, 2002) and is applied in standardized space

nodes.name: Classify the brain into CSF, gray matter, and white matter using an artificial neural network trained on tissue priors.

metadata.source_quote: The brain is classified into cerebrospinal fluid, gray matter, and white matter using an artificial neural network (ANN) trained on the intensities of the tissue priors

nodes.name: Mask blood vessels by detecting T1w hyperintensities with line morphology in sulci.

metadata.source_quote: it is critical to identify T1w hyperintensities, commonly representing major blood vessels and erroneously segmented as white matter by the classifier

nodes.name: Perform surface-based registration to the average surface template and resample cortical thickness maps.

metadata.source_quote: Surface-based registration is performed and the cortical thickness maps are blurred and resampled at the common vertex locations of the template

nodes.name: Quality control includes visual inspection of brain masks and surfaces for accuracy.

metadata.source_quote: The procedure proved to be very robust at extracting accurate masks on scans of individual subjects (see Fig. 2)

nodes.name: The N3 spline distance should be empirically determined to ensure uniform gray and white matter intensities.

metadata.source_quote: This value can be determined empirically such that the intensities for gray matter and white matter appear mostly uniform across the brain.

nodes.name: The pipeline is not validated for species other than macaques; adaptations for other primates would require appropriate length scales and templates.

metadata.source_quote: Further adaptations of the pipeline to other non-human primate brains should be straightforward by introducing the appropriate length scales and supplying species specific templates.

nodes.name: The NMT v2 is the current version; the paper describes NMT v1.2, so users should be aware of version differences.

metadata.source_quote: The NMT v2 is the most current version of this dataset.

nodes.name: The pipeline may require manual intervention for custom brain masks in rare registration failures.

metadata.source_quote: In the rare case when registration fails, a custom brain mask in native space can be supplied.

nodes.name: Cortical thickness maps calculated as the distance between the two cortical surfaces.

metadata.source_quote: Cortical thickness is calculated as the distance between the two cortical surfaces.

nodes.name: Surface-based registration results with resampled cortical thickness maps at template vertex locations.

metadata.source_quote: Surface-based registration is performed and the cortical thickness maps are blurred and resampled at the common vertex locations of the template

nodes.name: Outputs can be exported in NIfTI/GIfTI formats for integration with other tools.

metadata.source_quote: Full compatibility exists to read input T1w scans in NIfTI format and to export the outputs in the commonly used NIfTI/GIfTI formats

nodes.name: Length scale of 0.4 for all length-related parameters relative to human brain size.

metadata.source_quote: A length scale of 0.4 was derived from the cubic root of the macaque-to-human volume ratio

nodes.name: Processing voxel resolution of 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm.

metadata.source_quote: The macaque brain is resampled in linear standardized space at the processing voxel resolution of 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm

nodes.name: Macapype NHP anatomical processing pipeline
nodes.species_scope: macaque, marmoset, baboon, chimpanzee (as supported by -species option)

metadata.purpose: Process nonhuman primate (NHP) brain MRI data in BIDS format, including data preparation, brain extraction, and brain segmentation, with optional template-based processing and derivatives output.

nodes.name: Input data must be in BIDS format, with T1w and T2w images expected.

metadata.source_quote: All the data have to be in BIDS format to run properly

nodes.name: T1 weighted images are expected with the _T1w BIDS extension.

metadata.source_quote: _T1w (BIDS) extension is expected for T1 weighted images

nodes.name: T2 weighted images are expected with the _T2w BIDS extension.

metadata.source_quote: _T2w (BIDS) extension is expected for T2 weighted images

nodes.name: All files with the same extension (T1w or T2w) will be aligned to the first one and averaged.

metadata.source_quote: All files with the same extension (T1w or T2w) will be aligned to the first one and averaged

nodes.name: The -data parameter must point to an existing BIDS format directory.

metadata.source_quote: -data : path to your data dataset (existing BIDS format directory)

nodes.name: The -out parameter must point to an existing output path.

metadata.source_quote: -out : path to the output results (an existing path)

nodes.name: The -soft parameter must be either SPM or ANTS, with SPM requiring a specific version of macapype/skullTo3d not available by default.

metadata.source_quote: -soft : can be one of these : SPM or ANTS ( NB: SPM requires a specific version of macapype/skullTo3d, not available by default)

nodes.name: Either -params or -species must be provided; -params is mandatory if -species is omitted, and vice versa.

metadata.source_quote: -params : (mandatory if -species is omitted) a json file specifiying the global parameters of the analysis.

nodes.name: Run the main script segment_pnh.py as a Python script, or use the segment_pnh command if installed via pypi or container.

metadata.source_quote:
The main file is located in workflows and is called segment_pnh.py and should be called like a python script:
$ python workflows/segment_pnh.py

nodes.name: Specify the input data directory, output directory, and software choice (SPM or ANTS) as mandatory command line parameters.

metadata.source_quote:
-data : path to your data dataset (existing BIDS format directory)
-out : path to the output results (an existing path)
-soft : can be one of these : SPM or ANTS

nodes.name: Provide either a -params JSON file with global parameters or a -species option specifying the NHP species (e.g., macaque, marmo, baboon, chimp).

metadata.source_quote:
-params : (mandatory if -species is omitted) a json file specifiying the global parameters of the analysis. See Parameters for more details
-species : (mandatory if -params is omitted) followed the NHP species corresponding to the image, e.g. {macaque | marmo | baboon | chimp}

nodes.name: Optionally specify the datatype for brain segmentation using -dt, which can be 'T1' or 'T1 T2'; default is T1 if omitted.

metadata.source_quote:
-dt : specifies the datatype available to perform brain segmentation (can be “T1”, or “T1 T2”)
Note : default is T1 if the attribute is omitted

nodes.name: Optionally use -deriv to create a derivatives directory with important files named following BIDS derivatives convention.

metadata.source_quote: -deriv : creates a derivatives directory, with all important files, properly named following BIDS derivatives convertion.

nodes.name: Optionally use -padback to export most important files in native (original) space.

metadata.source_quote: -padback : exports most important files in native (original) space

nodes.name: Optionally specify a subset of the BIDS dataset using -sub, -ses, -acq, -rec, and control parallelism with -nprocs.

metadata.source_quote: -sub (-subjects), -ses (-sessions), -acq (-acquisions), -rec (-reconstructions) allows to specifiy a subset of the BIDS dataset respectively to a range of subjects, session, acquision types and reconstruction types.

nodes.name: The -test option can be used to check if the full pipeline is coherent, generating only graph.dot and graph.png.

metadata.source_quote: _test : (at the end) to check if the full pipeline is coherent (will only generate the graph.dot and graph.png)

nodes.name: The -prep option performs only data preparation, without brain extraction and segmentation.

metadata.source_quote: _prep (at the end) will perform data preparation (no brain extraction and segmentation)

nodes.name: The -noseg option performs data preparation and brain extraction, but no segmentation.

metadata.source_quote: _noseg (at the end) will perform data preparation and brain extraction (no segmentation)

nodes.name: The _4animal option uses bet4animal (FSL) for brain extraction, for faster computation; by default atlas_brex is used.

metadata.source_quote: _4animal : will use bet4animal (FSL) for brain extraction, for faster computation (by default atlas_brex is used)

nodes.name: The _quick option uses hd-bet (Deep Learning) for brain extraction, for faster computation; hd-bet requires a specific version of macapype/skullTo3d not available by default.

metadata.source_quote:
_quick : will use hd-bet (Deep Learning) for brain extraction, for faster computation (by default atlas_brex is used)
**NB: ** hd-bet requires a specific version of macapype/skullTo3d, not available by default

nodes.name: The _robustreg option should be used if coregistration to template in preparation is not performed correctly, providing a more robust registration in two steps.

metadata.source_quote:
This option should be used if the coregistration to template in preparation is not performed correctly:
_robustreg (at the end) to have a more robust registration (in two steps)

nodes.name: The marmoT2 species option can be used for segmenting from the T2w image; by default, T1w is used for marmo.

metadata.source_quote: NB : marmoT2 can be used for segmenting from the T2w image (by default, T1w is used for marmo)

nodes.name: Baboon templates baboon0, baboon1, baboon2, baboon3 can be used for template Baba21 and matching ages.

metadata.source_quote:
NB : baboon0, baboon1, baboon2 baboon3 can be used for template Baba21
and matching ages

nodes.name: Some templates are available in downgraded versions (e.g., baboon1_0p6, macaque_0p5) showing significant decrease in processing time with low reduction in quality, but not all combinations are available.

metadata.source_quote: NB : some templates are available in downgraded versions: baboon1_0p6, baboon2_0p6 baboon3_0p6 and macaque_0p5 and show significant decrease in processing time with low redection in quality. However, not all combinations are available

nodes.name: The pipeline can create a derivatives directory with all important files, properly named following BIDS derivatives convention.

metadata.source_quote: -deriv : creates a derivatives directory, with all important files, properly named following BIDS derivatives convertion.

nodes.name: The pipeline can export most important files in native (original) space using -padback.

metadata.source_quote: -padback : exports most important files in native (original) space

nodes.name: The -test option generates graph.dot and graph.png files to check pipeline coherence.

metadata.source_quote: _test : (at the end) to check if the full pipeline is coherent (will only generate the graph.dot and graph.png)

nodes.name: The -indiv or -indiv_params parameter allows a JSON file to overwrite default parameters for specific subjects/sessions.

metadata.source_quote: -indiv or -indiv_params : a json file overwriting the default parameters (both macapype default and parameters specified in -params json file) for specific subjects/sessions.

nodes.name: The -params parameter specifies a JSON file with global parameters of the analysis, mandatory if -species is omitted.

metadata.source_quote: -params : (mandatory if -species is omitted) a json file specifiying the global parameters of the analysis.

nodes.name: The -species parameter specifies the NHP species corresponding to the image, e.g., macaque, marmo, baboon, chimp; mandatory if -params is omitted.

metadata.source_quote: -species : (mandatory if -params is omitted) followed the NHP species corresponding to the image, e.g. {macaque | marmo | baboon | chimp}

nodes.name: Sequence Adaptive Multimodal SEGmentation (SAMSEG)
nodes.species_scope: human (implied by brain MRI and MS context)

metadata.purpose: Robustly segment dozens of brain structures from head MRI scans without preprocessing, accepting multi-contrast data without prior assumptions on scanner or pulse sequences.

nodes.name: One or more co-registered MRI volumes in Nifti (.nii/.nii.gz) or FreeSurfer (.mgz) format.

metadata.source_quote: takes one or more co-registered MRI volumes as input

nodes.name: All input volumes must be co-registered with each other and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.

metadata.source_quote: the only requirement is that all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

nodes.name: For multi-contrast data, it is recommended to select the contrast with the highest spatial resolution and reformat all other contrasts to that grid.

metadata.source_quote: it is recommended to select the contrast with the highest spatial resolution (smallest voxel size) and reformat all other contrasts to that

nodes.name: For longitudinal processing, all time points must be co-registered and reformatted to the same image grid, using an unbiased reference template.

metadata.source_quote: longitudinal SAMSEG expects all its input images to have been co-registered and reformatted to the same image grid beforehand

nodes.name: Preprocessing with FreeSurfer is neither required nor recommended for basic SAMSEG.

metadata.source_quote: Preprocessing of the scan(s) with FreeSurfer is neither required nor recommended

nodes.name: For multi-contrast input, all volumes must be co-registered and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.

metadata.source_quote: all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

nodes.name: For longitudinal SAMSEG, the same combination of contrasts must be provided for each time point.

metadata.source_quote: SAMSEG expects that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point

nodes.name: When using the lesion flag, the lesion-mask-pattern is optional but strongly recommended.

metadata.source_quote: --lesion-mask-pattern <pattern> (optional but strongly recommended)

nodes.name: Run run_samseg with --input specifying one or more co-registered MRI volumes and --output specifying the output directory.

metadata.source_quote: run_samseg --input <file> [<file> ...] --output <dir>

nodes.name: Optionally set --threads to the number of CPU cores for faster run time.

metadata.source_quote: Set the number of threads to the number of CPU cores on your computer to get the fastest run time

nodes.name: Add --pallidum-separate if the input contrasts include those where the pallidum is clearly discernible, e.g., T2w or FLAIR.

metadata.source_quote: if your combination of input volumes includes contrasts where the pallidum is clearly discernible (e.g., T2w or FLAIR) you should add this flag

nodes.name: For MS lesion segmentation, add --lesion and optionally --lesion-mask-pattern with one number per input contrast.

metadata.source_quote: --lesion: is the flag to tell SAMSEG to segment white matter lesions

nodes.name: For longitudinal processing, first compute a robust average template using mri_robust_template, then run run_samseg_long with --timepoint for each time point.

metadata.source_quote: mri_robust_template --mov tp0_t1.nii tp1_t1.nii tp2_t1.nii --template mean.mgz --satit --mapmov tp0_t1_reg.mgz tp1_t1_reg.mgz tp2_t1_reg.mgz

nodes.name: For multi-contrast longitudinal data, co-register each additional contrast to the corresponding reformatted T1w scan using mri_coreg and mri_vol2vol.

metadata.source_quote: for each time additionally co-registering each FLAIR scan to the corresponding reformatted T1w scan

nodes.name: For longitudinal MS patients, add the same lesion flags as in cross-sectional processing.

metadata.source_quote: Segmenting white matter lesions in MS with longitudinal SAMSEG is accomplished simply by adding the same flags as for the cross-sectional version

nodes.name: Verify that all input volumes are co-registered and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.

metadata.source_quote: the only requirement is that all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

nodes.name: For longitudinal processing, ensure that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point.

metadata.source_quote: SAMSEG expects that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point

nodes.name: When using the lesion flag, verify that the lesion-mask-pattern has one number for each input contrast.

metadata.source_quote: The pattern is a sequence of numbers, one number for each input contrast

nodes.name: The pallidum is treated internally as a white matter structure by default because it typically cannot be discerned easily from white matter in T1w scans.

metadata.source_quote: by default SAMSEG will treat the pallidum internally as a white matter structure, since it typically can't be discerned easily from white matter in T1w scans

nodes.name: The first time the MS lesion module is run, the user may be prompted to install Tensorflow.

metadata.source_quote: The first time you run this module, you may be prompted to install Tensorflow

nodes.name: For longitudinal processing, simply reformatting all follow-up time points to the baseline scan would introduce a longitudinal processing bias.

metadata.source_quote: simply reformatting all follow-up time points to the baseline scan would introduce a longitudinal processing bias

nodes.name: seg.mgz: output segmentation volume where each voxel is assigned to one anatomical structure.

metadata.source_quote: seg.mgz: is the output segmentation volume, where each voxel has been assigned to one anatomical structure

nodes.name: samseg.stats: contains the estimated volume in cubic mm for each segmented structure.

metadata.source_quote: samseg.stats: contains the estimated volume (in cubic mm) for each segmented structure

nodes.name: mode0X_bias_corrected.mgz: the bias field corrected MRI volume corresponding to each input contrast.

metadata.source_quote: mode0X_bias_corrected.mgz (with X=1,2,...): the bias field corrected MRI volume corresponding to each input contrast

nodes.name: mode0X_bias_field.mgz: the estimated bias field for each input contrast.

metadata.source_quote: mode0X_bias_field.mgz (with X=1,2,...): the estimated bias field for each input contrast

nodes.name: --threads: number of threads to be used by SAMSEG; default uses one thread.

metadata.source_quote: <threads> (optional): is the number of threads to be used by SAMSEG (default uses one thread)

nodes.name: --pallidum-separate: optional flag to treat the pallidum as a separate structure when contrasts make it discernible.

metadata.source_quote: --pallidum-separate (optional): by default SAMSEG will treat the pallidum internally as a white matter structure

nodes.name: --lesion-mask-pattern: optional but strongly recommended; a sequence of numbers, one per input contrast, indicating intensity constraints relative to cortical gray matter.

metadata.source_quote: The pattern is a sequence of numbers, one number for each input contrast, with the following meaning: a value of "-1" or "1" indicates the voxels should be darker or brighter than cortical gray matter

nodes.name: --threshold: optional threshold applied to the probability of a voxel being lesion; default is 0.3 in the current implementation.

metadata.source_quote: The default value (0.3 in the current implementation) will typically give reasonable results

nodes.name: FreeSurfer Cortical Reconstruction Failure Mode Identification and QC Workflow

metadata.purpose: Identify cortical reconstruction failures and determine appropriate quality control and repair stages in the FreeSurfer recon-all pipeline.

nodes.name: T1-weighted anatomical image(s) in DICOM or other native scanner format.

metadata.source_quote: the raw data from the scan must be converted into a format recognized by FreeSurfer

nodes.name: Subject directory created via recon-all -i command.

metadata.source_quote: recon-all -i <path-to-first-structural> [-i <path-to-second-structural>] -s <subjid>

nodes.name: Output volumes from recon-all processing, including T1.mgz, brainmask.mgz, and surface files.

metadata.source_quote: load the T1 and brainmask images as underlays in freeview, and overlay the white and pial surfaces

nodes.name: Anatomical data should have good quality: strong contrast between tissue types, no movement, high resolution.

metadata.source_quote: If your anatomical data is of good quality - strong contrast between the tissue types, no movement, high resolution

nodes.name: Soft failures occur when recon-all finishes without errors but output has obvious errors needing fixes.

metadata.source_quote: Soft Failures, on the other hand, occur when recon-all has finished without any errors - but upon closer observation of the output there are obvious errors

nodes.name: Run recon-all -autorecon1 and stop to check for problems with intensity normalization, talairach transformation, and skull stripping.

metadata.source_quote:
recon-all -subjid <subject name> -autorecon1
stop to check for problems with intensity normalization, talairach transformation and skull stripping

nodes.name: Run recon-all -autorecon2 and stop to check final surfaces and make appropriate edits.

metadata.source_quote:
recon-all -subjid <subject name> -autorecon2
stop to check final surfaces and make appropriate edits

nodes.name: If the WM volume was edited, run recon-all -autorecon2-wm; if control points were added, run -autorecon2-cp; if the BRAIN volume was edited, run -autorecon2-pial.

metadata.source_quote:
if:
the WM volume was edited: recon-all -subjid <subject name> -autorecon2-wm
control points were added: recon-all -subjid <subject name> -autorecon2-cp
the BRAIN volume was edited: recon-all -subjid <subject name> -autorecon2-pial

nodes.name: Run recon-all -autorecon3 to complete the processing after any edits.

metadata.source_quote: recon-all -subjid <subject name> -autorecon3

nodes.name: Load T1 and brainmask images as underlays in freeview, overlay white and pial surfaces for both hemispheres.

metadata.source_quote:
freeview -v [subject]/mri/T1.mgz \
[subject]/mri/brainmask.mgz \
-f [subject]/surf/lh.pial:edgecolor=red \
[subject]/surf/lh.white:edgecolor=yellow \
[subject]/surf/rh.pial:edgecolor=red \
[subject]/surf/rh.white:edgecolor=yellow

nodes.name: Visually inspect slices for anomalies, noting that anomalies resolving in adjacent slices may be projection artifacts and not require editing.

metadata.source_quote: If the anomaly resolves in the next slice or two, that is probably because the white matter is being projected in a direction orthogonal to the slice

nodes.name: Ignore surfaces drawn in the medial wall near ventricles and corpus callosum, and near subcortical structures, as they are not used in final surface calculations.

metadata.source_quote: the surfaces drawn in the medial wall near the ventricles and corpus callosum, and the surfaces drawn near the subcortical structures, will not be used in the final surface calculations and can be ignored during editing.

nodes.name: Perform manual edits using erasing voxels, filling voxels, adding control points, or cloning voxels as needed.
Check for soft failures: large holes in white matter, pial surface errors, skullstripping errors, intensity normalization errors, topological defects, and white matter segmentation errors.
Verify that surfaces follow the true boundaries of gray and white matter by visual inspection.

metadata.source_quote: Make sure that the surfaces follow the true boundaries of the top and bottom of the gray matter.

nodes.name: Small and infrequent discrepancies between FreeSurfer-drawn borders and actual gray/white borders should be left alone, as editing may worsen the problem.

metadata.source_quote: as long as the discrepancies are relatively small and infrequent, it’s best to leave them alone. In those cases, sometimes editing the surfaces can make the problem worse, not better.

nodes.name: White matter segmentation errors caused by lesions or gliomas are relatively uncommon in healthy subjects and are not covered in the tutorial.

metadata.source_quote: These are relatively uncommon in healthy subjects, and will not be covered in this course.

nodes.name: Topological defects are very rare since FreeSurfer version 6.0 and are usually automatically fixed during recon-all.

metadata.source_quote: Since the release of FreeSurfer version 6.0 these types of errors are very rare, and they are usually automatically fixed during recon-all.

nodes.name: For populations where aseg tools are ineffective (e.g., monkey or newborn data), use the -noaseg flag to skip subcortical segmentation.

metadata.source_quote: If you are working with a population for which the aseg tools will not be effective, e.g., monkey data and newborn data, use the flag -noaseg.
